A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same heterogeneous-GPU LLM serving study. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison. V1's Appendices A–K are retained in v2, which adds Appendices L–M.

before.justification: Sections 3 and 5 and the appendices report original GPU benchmarks, throughput and latency measurements, ablations, and scheduling-efficiency experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds Helix comparisons, profiling validation, and workload-change and GPU-loss replanning results in Tables 3, 6 and 7.

M1.justification: The written makespan calculation now multiplies assignment fractions by workload request counts in Equations (3) and (9), correcting their omission in v1. The MILP framework, heuristics and binary search remain intact. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: The existing datasets and serving tasks are retained. Appendix M adds explicit dynamic scenarios involving a surge in short-output requests and the loss of four H100 GPUs, extending evaluation beyond the previously reported workload mixtures and availability snapshots.

E2.justification: Helix, previously discussed as related work, becomes an evaluated comparator in Table 3. The existing HexGen comparisons, homogeneous RTX 4090/RTX A6000/H100 baselines, and ablation alternatives are retained.

E3.justification: The new Helix experiment uses its single-cluster setup on AzureTrace at $15/hour and adds a Llama-30B model configuration. Appendix M introduces a $30/hour before/after/replanning evaluation. Existing benchmark metrics, trace mixtures and hardware settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix L adds measured-versus-estimated throughput comparisons across seven configurations to assess profiling accuracy. Appendix M tests degradation and recovery after workload changes and GPU loss. Existing component ablations, solver-efficiency and budget analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Appendix L's new prediction-error discussion assesses estimator accuracy and does not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark results are retained. New Table 3 reports ours/Helix throughput of 11.43/8.49 req/s for Llama-30B and 7.13/5.72 for Llama3-70B. Tables 6–7 add profiling and replanning results, including recovery from 23.70 to 29.61 and 20.80 to 22.85 req/s. These are additional experiments, not demonstrated same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix E introduce request-count factors into the makespan expressions. Section 4.3 also adds a worst-case complexity argument, O(poly(|C|,W,N) × 2^|C|). That argument calls activation variables binary although Equation (7) retains their nonnegative-integer domain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: heterogeneous-GPU cost-efficiency benchmarking and joint optimization of GPU composition, deployment configurations and workload assignment. The headline throughput and latency claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix M newly identifies online scheduling as outside the central approach, discusses adapting through replanning, and explains cost-efficiency versus latency tradeoffs and queuing effects. Appendix L adds the interpretation that profiling estimates are sufficiently accurate for configuration selection.

D1.justification: V1 only mentions one-time profiling. Appendix L documents profiling individual transformer layers across GPU types and TP degrees, measuring pipeline communication, combining costs, and treating prefill and decoding batching separately. This clarifies how existing throughput estimates are obtained.

R1.justification: A new background paragraph distinguishes the approach from QLM, SarathiServe and Vidur, and Appendix L credits Vidur's profiling approach. The bibliography adds works including FlashFlex, ThunderServe and HexGen-2. Existing research positioning remains largely intact; publication-metadata updates do not represent new works.

P1.justification: Most prose and the six-section main narrative are retained. V2 adds local headings and explanations, Appendices L–M, impact and acknowledgment sections, and updates equal-contribution markings and publication information.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 3, 6 and 7 and a request-count row in Table 2. Benchmark axes clarify throughput per dollar and deployment configurations; Figure 3's caption is expanded. Figures are resized or relocated, and existing appendix tables are renumbered, while the established visual organization is retained.

improvement.justification: The request-count corrections, profiling documentation and validation, Helix comparison, and replanning tests address specific gaps in v1. These yield a limited net improvement in clarity and evidential support. New inconsistencies constrain the gain: Table 6's 0.42 versus 0.46 req/s exceeds the stated 4–7% error range, Table 7 misstates percentage decreases, and the complexity argument assumes binary variables despite their integer definitions.
